question: Three water pipes m, n and p, take 5, 6 and 12 hours, respectively, to fill a water tank. If all three pipes are opened at the same time, then the required time to fill the water tank will be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
**Total Work** = LCM of 5, 6, and 12 = 60 units.

**Efficiencies**: m = 12, n = 10, p = 5.

**Combined Efficiency** = 12 + 10 + 5 = 27 units/hr.

**Time required** = 60 ÷ 27 = 20 ÷ 9 = 2 2/9 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 2/9 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Pipe m = 5 hr, Pipe n = 6 hr, Pipe p = 12 hr.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Time × Efficiency

 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency**
 **m** 5 60 12
 **n** 6 10
 **p** 12 5
**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Efficiency of **(m + n + p)** = 12 + 10 + 5 = 27 units/hr

⇒ Total Time Taken = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time = 60 ÷ 27

⇒ Time = 20 ÷ 9

⇒ Time = 2 2/9 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 2 2/9 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Combined Work Formula**

If two pipes fill a tank in x and y hours, they together fill it in (xy)/(x+y) hours.

**Pipes and Cisterns Rule**

Efficiency of an **inlet pipe** is positive, while efficiency of an **outlet (leak) pipe** is negative.

**Alternate Filling**

If pipes operate on alternate hours, calculate the work done in one **cycle** (sum of their efficiencies) and then find the total cycles.</p
